extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory/regulatory requirements for provisional, nonprovisional, continuation/divisional filings, correction of inventorship, and related filing/conversion procedures before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.48. Correction of inventorship in a patent application, other than a reissue application, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information may be required. "The Office may require such other information as may be deemed appropriate under the particular circumstances surrounding the correction of inventorship." (37 CFR 1.48(g)). See related MPEP sections for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: National-stage inventorship correction exception
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.48(f)(1) is not applicable for national stage applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 371 where the inventorship has been erroneously named in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventorship in the oath/declaration filed in the national stage differs from the international application, the requirements of 37 CFR 1.497(d) must be satisfied. See MPEP § 1893.01(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent application definition and benefit (35 U.S.C. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'parent' is applied to an earlier application of an inventor disclosing a given invention; benefit of the filing date of a copending parent application may be claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120. The term 'parent' will not be used to describe a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parent application may or may not claim the invention; to receive benefit the applications must satisfy statutory/ regulatory conditions (see MPEP § 201.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original application definition
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Original' refers to an application which is not a reissue application; an original application may be a first filing or a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in statute and rules to distinguish reissue practice from initial/continuing filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application authorization and content (35 U.S.C. 111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must be made or authorized to be made by the inventor and must include (A) a specification as prescribed by the first paragraph of section 112, and (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional must contain a written description meeting 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph and any required drawings per 37 CFR 1.81(a). The filing date is the date these items are received (see 37 CFR 1.53(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No claim and no oath required in a provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim (second through fifth paragraphs of section 112) shall not be required in a provisional application. No oath or declaration is required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE in MPEP: (A) No claim is required. (B) No oath or declaration is required. However, to convert to or benefit a nonprovisional certain additional formalities will be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application fee submission and abandonment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee may be submitted after the specification and any required drawing are submitted, within such period and under such conditions (including a surcharge) as prescribed by the Director. Failure to submit the fee within such prescribed period results in abandonment unless delay was unavoidable or unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment procedures, surcharge possibilities, and revival limitations are set forth in statute/regulation. Applicants who miss fee deadlines must show delay was unavoidable or unintentional to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional filing date and cover sheet requirement (37 CFR 1.53(c) / 1.51(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which the specification (complying with 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph) and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a) are filed in the PTO. A provisional must also include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) (may be an application data sheet or cover letter identifying the application as provisional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the cover sheet is missing, the application will be treated as filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (nonprovisional) rather than as a provisional. No amendment other than to make it comply with statute/regulations may be made after the provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional conversion rules and consequences (conversion to/from nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraph (b) (nonprovisional) may be converted to a provisional application and accorded the original filing date if a request for conversion and processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(q)) are filed prior to certain events. A provisional filed under paragraph (c) may be converted to a nonprovisional provided conversion request, fees, and an amendment including at least one claim (per 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph) are filed and other fees and an oath/declaration are supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion timing constraints: must be filed before the earliest of abandonment of the application, payment of issue fee, expiration of 12 months after the filing date, or filing of a request for a statutory invention registration. Conversion to nonprovisional does not entitle applicant to refund of earlier fees and may have adverse patent term impacts (term measured from at least filing date of the provisional). To avoid patent-term adverse effects, applicants should consider filing a nonprovisional that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) rather than converting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application lacks priority/benefit rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall not be entitled to the right of priority of any other application under section 119 or 365(a) or to the benefit of an earlier filing date in the United States under section 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No claim for priority under 35 U.S.C.119(e) or §1.78(a)(4) may be made in a design application based on a provisional application. If a provisional improperly states benefit of an earlier application, the filing receipt will not reflect that improper benefit. If a nonprovisional claims benefit of a provisional and states that the provisional relies on an earlier application, the earlier-than-provisional benefit claim will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application limitations (examination, interferences, SIR, sequence rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications will not be examined for patentability, placed in an interference, or made the subject of a statutory invention registration. The requirements of §§1.821–1.825 regarding nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures are not mandatory for provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional is essentially a priority placeholder with limited formal procedures; do not expect examination or placement in interference and certain specialized disclosure rules do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of application types (37 CFR 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: (1) 'national application' means a U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 or entering national stage after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371; (2) 'provisional application' means a U.S. national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b); (3) 'nonprovisional application' means a U.S. national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or entering national stage after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correctly classifying the application type is critical because different filing, content, and procedural rules apply to each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional application filing requirements (37 CFR 1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C.112 containing a description pursuant to §1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to §1.75, and any drawing required by §1.81(a) are filed in the PTO. No new matter may be introduced after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing applications (continuation, divisional, CIP) may be filed under conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) and §1.78(a). Ensure required claims and description are present to secure a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application definition and benefit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application is a later application for an independent or distinct invention carved out of a pending application and disclosing and claiming only subject matter disclosed in the earlier or parent application. The divisional must claim the benefit of the prior nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 121 or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The divisional should set forth at least the portion of the earlier disclosure germane to the invention as claimed. Do not introduce new matter or vary disclosure in substance from the parent. See MPEP §201.11 for conditions to receive the benefit of the parent's filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional filing procedures and classification suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility or plant divisionals must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Design divisionals may be filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d). Applicants are requested to include the appropriate USPTO classification and the status/assigned art unit of the parent on papers to expedite processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place classification designation in the upper right corner of the transmittal letter or in an application data sheet per 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3). Use form paragraph 2.01 to remind applicants of possible divisional status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional limitations regarding provisional applications and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming the benefits of a provisional under 35 U.S.C.119(e) should not be called a 'division' of the provisional. A divisional may depart in phraseology from the parent but may not depart in substance or introduce matter that would be 'new matter' in the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional patent term and entitlement differ from provisional-derived filings—careful drafting and correct labeling are required to avoid loss of benefit or incorrect patent-term calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design divisional special rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A design application may be considered a division of a utility application (but not of a provisional) and is entitled to the filing date of the utility application if the drawings of the earlier filed utility application show the same article as that in the design application sufficiently to comply with 35 U.S.C.112, first paragraph. Such a divisional design application must be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), not under 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1504.20 for detailed conditions; ensure drawings in the utility application clearly show the same article to secure entitlement to the earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration practice for continuation/divisional applications (37 CFR 1.63(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration is not required in a continuation or divisional application provided: (i) the prior nonprovisional contained a prescribed oath/declaration; (ii) the continuation/divisional was filed by all or fewer than all inventors named in the prior application; (iii) the specification and drawings contain no matter that would have been new matter in the prior application; and (iv) a copy of the executed oath/declaration filed in the prior application, showing the signature or an indication thereon that it was signed, is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy of the executed oath/declaration must be accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of any person(s) not inventors in the continuation/divisional. If the prior application had §1.47 status, additional documentation (copy of decision granting petition to accord §1.47 status) must accompany the copy unless all inventors or legal representatives have filed an oath/declaration to join in an application accorded §1.47 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of filings under former 37 CFR 1.60 / 1.62
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.60 and 1.62 were deleted effective December 1, 1997. A continuation or divisional filed under former 1.60 on or after that date will be treated as filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Requests filed under former 1.62 on or after December 1, 1997 in certain circumstances will be treated as requests for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 or as improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation/divisional/CIP applications filed under former rules prior to deletion continue to be processed under the old procedures. Consult MPEP §201.06(a)/(b) and MPEP 706.07(h) for handling depending on filing date and facts.
